title: Quant Preset Handoff: Calibration Orchestrator, Shadow Validation & Canary Rollback Plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define the end-to-end engineering handoff and implementation plan for per-model quantization defaults in the model catalog. This ticket centralizes the orchestration components, dataset sampling/calibration workflows, shadow validation metrics, and a conservative canary + rollback policy for FP8/INT8 presets.
background: PMs and catalog owners have asked for recommended quantization defaults per model (fp8/int8 presets) that can be applied automatically at deployment time. We need a reproducible calibration flow and safety net to catch accuracy regressions before wide rollout. Prior work provided policy templates and tooling, but operational orchestration and concrete rollback criteria are missing.
goals: Ship a reproducible calibration orchestration blueprint that can be executed for each catalog model
Provide automated shadow validation that computes accuracy/perplexity deltas and synthetic safety signals for candidate quant profiles
Define canary rollout gates and rollback triggers that are conservative by default and configurable per customer tier
Instrument observability and dashboards for calibration runs and canaries (latency/cost/quality)
success_metrics: <= 1.0% median downstream metric regression (task-dependent) comparing quantized vs fp32 on validation sets
< 0.5% of production requests hit an automatic rollback post-canary in the first 14 days
Calibration runs complete within target wall-clock time (model-size dependent): small < 2h, medium < 6h, large < 24h
Automated shadow validation coverage >= 90% of curated eval prompt sets for the model
calibration_strategy: Stratified shard-aware sampling of customer-like prompt distributions, per-layer activation histogram collection, outlier clip handling, and per-head statistics for transformers. Default flow: 1) collect representative samples (10k-100k tokens depending on model class), 2) run offline calibration on candidate quant schemas (INT8 symmetric/asymmetric, FP8 variants), 3) produce per-layer quant params and a calibration signature artifact stored in catalog.
orchestration_components: shadow-run scheduler (routes 0% traffic to quant variant for validation)
validation-harness (eval runner with regression checks + metric extraction)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Local calibration artifact generation and unit tests (engineering)
Stage 1: Shadow validation in staging (zero production traffic) against curated eval sets
Stage 2: Canary rollout to 0.5% traffic with shadow runs running in parallel; monitor metrics for 48 hours
Stage 3: If canary passes, expand to 5% for 3 days, then 25% for 7 days before wide rollout
Stage 4: Full rollout only after automated acceptance and PM signoff; document in catalog entry
rollback_criteria: Any downstream task with relative metric degradation > 1.5% (configurable per-model) in shadow validation
Perplexity increase > 2.5% on language-model test suites
Sustained 99th percentile latency regression > 20% for the quantized path vs baseline
Manual override by catalog owner or SRE if false positives observed
observability_and_alerting: Calibration run dashboard (duration, sample coverage, per-layer quant stats)
Shadow validation dashboard (metric deltas, sample-level failure cases, token-level perplexity distributions)
Canary alerting: slack + pager on severity if rollback criteria met
Retention of calibration artifacts and diffs for 90 days
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Calibration dataset not representative -> Mitigation: shard-aware sampling and weekly sampling drift check
Risk: FP8 numerical corner cases -> Mitigation: add per-layer fallback to INT8 and conservative clipping heuristics
Risk: Shadow validation blind spots -> Mitigation: include adversarial and high-sensitivity prompts in eval sets and surface sample-level failures
Risk: Canary oscillations under noisy traffic -> Mitigation: use smoothing windows and require persistence across multiple windows before triggering rollback

acceptance_criteria: Calibration-orchestrator can run end-to-end and produce a catalog artifact with per-layer quant params
Shadow validation produces a reproducible report with metric deltas and retained raw samples for inspection
Canary-controller successfully rolls forward and rolls back based on the defined gates in a staged test environment
Runbook written with steps for manual rollback and postmortem checklist linked in the catalog entry
